title: Post-op Blood Pressure Trend
scenario: A 40-year-old client is recovering on the surgical unit four hours after an exploratory laparotomy. Vital signs are recorded every 30 minutes.

tabs.title: Post-op Vital Signs
rows: Restless. Dressing with small serosanguineous spot.
Pale, cool skin. Dressing saturated with bright red blood.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which interpretation of the vital sign trend is correct?

options.text: Falling blood pressure with rising pulse suggests hypovolemic shock from hemorrhage
The trend reflects an expected, stable post-operative recovery
The findings indicate a vasovagal response that will self-resolve
Rising blood pressure indicates pain-related hypertension

questions.rationale: The progressive fall in blood pressure with a compensatory rising heart rate, plus pallor and a saturated dressing, are classic signs of hypovolemic shock from postoperative hemorrhage.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse take now? Select all that apply.

options.text: Apply direct pressure to the bleeding site and reinforce the dressing
Increase the IV fluid rate as ordered
Place the client flat and elevate the legs
Document the finding and reassess in one hour
Encourage the client to ambulate to improve circulation

questions.rationale: Suspected hemorrhage requires urgent surgeon notification, direct pressure and dressing reinforcement, increased fluids, and positioning to support perfusion. Delaying reassessment or ambulating the client would be unsafe.
